rationale:
The migrated public issue (dart-archive/yaml#49 -> dart-lang/tools#1906, 'Spans aren't correct for list nodes with a null value') supplies a concrete reproducer showing that an empty block-sequence entry reports a span pointing at the following entry's line. The production fix in lib/src/parser.dart captures the blockEntry token as prevToken before _scanner.advance() and passes prevToken.span.end to _processEmptyScalar instead of the advanced token's span.end, which is exactly the off-by-one-token span origin described in the issue. The minimized production patch is a single three-line hunk in one file with no refactor, formatting, docs, config, or feature change; the changelog/pubspec and later PR commits were excluded. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same fixing commit and uses only pre-existing public API (loadYaml, YamlList.nodes, span highlighting) with no API introduced by the fix. Strict machine evidence passes all gates both originally and post-minimization: build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential with reproduced selector test/span_test.dart::null nodes span, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green, over a complete 38-run matrix with 3 repetitions. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this root cause duplicates no active registry entry, and the key matches allowed_root_cause_ids.

The linked issue (dart-archive/yaml#49, migrated to dart-lang/tools#1906, 'Spans aren't correct for list nodes with a null value') reproduces with '- foo\n- \n- bar' where the null entry's span highlight points at the following '- bar' line. The minimized production patch matches that root cause exactly: in Parser._parseBlockSequenceEntry, the empty scalar's span was built from the token returned by _scanner.advance() (the next block entry / block end) instead of the blockEntry token itself; the fix captures prevToken before advancing and passes prevToken.span.end. The minimized patch equals the production-fix patch: one file, one hunk, three lines, no refactor, formatting, docs, config, or API change (the later PR commits that touched CHANGELOG/pubspec and reworked the fix to use 'start' are excluded from this revision pair). The trigger is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same commit and uses only pre-existing public API (loadYaml, YamlList.nodes, YamlNode.span, existing _expectSpan helper), so it introduces no dependency on new production API. Strict machine evidence reports both revisions build, the buggy revision fails exactly test/span_test.dart::'null nodes span' in isolation and in the full suite with deterministic fingerprints over 3 repetitions, and the fixed revision is all green including reversed runs. The active same-project root-cause registry is empty, so this root cause is not a duplicate.

risks: Two selectors are declared but only 'null nodes span' reproduces the defect; 'root nodes span' asserts spans for non-null nodes and passes on both revisions, so it adds no discriminating value and should not be treated as a defect trigger.

The trigger asserts source_span highlight() output containing box-drawing characters and depends on meaningful trailing whitespace in the YAML fixture; a different source_span resolution or whitespace-normalizing checkout could cause failures unrelated to the defect.

Traceability rests on an archived-issue redirect (yaml#49 -> tools#1906) rather than a directly fetchable issue in the origin repository; the mapping is asserted in case.json metadata rather than independently re-verified here.
Issue tools#1906 carries no explicit defect label; defect status is inferred from the reproducer body and the fix commit message.
